# Building the Complement

All the pieces now combine. Because $\approx_{\mathcal A}$ is a finite-index congruence that **saturates** $L(\mathcal A)$, and the Ramsey decomposition writes every $\omega$-word as some class product $U\,V^{\omega}$ (with $V$ idempotent), each such product is **entirely inside** $L(\mathcal A)$ or **entirely disjoint** from it. The complement is then just the union of the disjoint ones:
$$ \overline{L(\mathcal A)} \;=\; \bigcup\bigl\{\,U\,V^{\omega} \;:\; U\,V^{\omega}\cap L(\mathcal A)=\emptyset \,\bigr\}, $$
a **finite** union. The classes can be enumerated, their products formed, and each intersection with $L(\mathcal A)$ tested for emptiness — an *effective* construction.

We test products on the chapter's automaton $\mathcal A$ (accepts "$ab$ infinitely often, separated by $c$'s"). Pick a prefix $U$ and an idempotent block $V$; the widget runs the representative $u\cdot v^{\omega}$ and reports whether that whole product sits in $L$ or in $\overline{L}$.

> **A note on the running example.** The chapter's Example on saturation states $\alpha=a(abc)^{\omega}$ is accepted with $U=[a]$. On the *deterministic* $\mathcal A$ that run actually **dies** — after $a$ the automaton is in $s_1$, which has no outgoing $a$. The correct accepted witness is $ab(abc)^{\omega}$, i.e. $U=[ab]$ (the prefix must reach $s_2$, where the $abc$-block loops). The widget below uses that verified witness.

```{=html}
      <label>Preset</label>
      <select id="nb24-preset">
        <option value="0">U=[ab], V=[abc]</option>

  <div class="sc-panel">

<script>
(function(){
  const delta={ s0:{a:'s1'}, s1:{b:'s2'}, s2:{c:'s2',a:'s1'} };
  const F=new Set(['s1']); const init='s0';
  const parse=s=>s.trim().replace(/\s|,/g,'').split('').filter(x=>x.length);
  function runProduct(u,v,cycles=3){
    const seq=u.concat(...Array(cycles).fill(v));
    let state=init; const steps=[{sym:'',state}]; const tail=new Set(); let dead=false;
    for(let i=0;i<seq.length;i++){
      const nxt=delta[state]&&delta[state][seq[i]];
      if(nxt===undefined){ steps.push({sym:seq[i],state:'✗',dead:true}); dead=true; break; }
      state=nxt; steps.push({sym:seq[i],state}); if(i>=u.length) tail.add(state);
    }
    const accepted = !dead && [...tail].some(q=>F.has(q));
    return {steps,accepted,dead,tail:[...tail]};
  }
  function drawRun(steps){
    const strip=document.getElementById('nb24-strip'); strip.innerHTML='';
    steps.forEach(s=>{const box=document.createElement('div');box.className='run-step';
      const sy=document.createElement('div');sy.className='run-sym';sy.innerHTML=s.sym===''?'&nbsp;':s.sym;
      const st=document.createElement('div');st.className='run-state'+(s.dead?' dead':(F.has(s.state)?' accept':''));
      st.innerHTML=s.dead?'&#10007;':'s<sub>'+s.state[1]+'</sub>';
      box.appendChild(sy);box.appendChild(st);strip.appendChild(box);});
  }
  function classify(u,v){ return runProduct(u,v).accepted ? 'L' : 'C'; }
  const PRODUCTS=[['ab','abc'],['ab','c'],['a','abc'],['','abc'],['','c']];
  function go(){
    const u=parse(document.getElementById('nb24-u').value), v=parse(document.getElementById('nb24-v').value);
    const vd=document.getElementById('nb24-verdict');
    if(!v.length){vd.innerHTML="<div class='verdict-box verdict-C'>Block v cannot be empty.</div>";return;}
    for(const w of [u,v]) for(const s of w) if(!['a','b','c'].includes(s)){vd.innerHTML=`<div class='verdict-box verdict-C'>Unknown symbol "${s}". Alphabet is {a,b,c}.</div>`;return;}
    const r=runProduct(u,v); drawRun(r.steps);
    const inL=r.accepted;
    vd.innerHTML=`<div class="verdict-box ${inL?'verdict-L':'verdict-C'}"><strong>U·Vω = [${u.join('')||'ε'}]·[${v.join('')}]ω ⊆ ${inL?'L(𝒜)':'L(𝒜)ᶜ (the complement)'}.</strong><br>`+
      (inL ? `In(ρ)∩F = { s₁ } — the run threads through s₁∈F in every block, so the whole product is accepted.`
           : (r.dead ? `The run dies (a missing transition), so no word of this product is accepted — the product lies entirely in the complement.`
                     : `In(ρ) = { ${r.tail.map(x=>'s'+x[1]).join(', ')} }, disjoint from F — no accepting state recurs, so the whole product lies in the complement.`))+`</div>`;
    // enumerate table
    const tbl=document.getElementById('nb24-table');
    tbl.innerHTML='<tr><th>class product</th><th>witness u·vω</th><th>run</th><th>side</th></tr>';
    const comp=[];
    for(const [pu,pv] of PRODUCTS){
      const rr=runProduct(pu,pv); const side=rr.accepted?'L':'C'; if(side==='C')comp.push(`[${pu||'ε'}]·[${pv}]ω`);
      tbl.innerHTML+=`<tr><td>[${pu||'ε'}]·[${pv}]ω</td><td>${(pu||'ε')}·(${pv})ω</td><td>${rr.accepted?'accepts':(rr.dead?'dies':'no F recurs')}</td><td><span class="tag ${side}">${side==='L'?'L(𝒜)':'complement'}</span></td></tr>`;
    }
    document.getElementById('nb24-formula').innerHTML=`L(𝒜)ᶜ &supe; &nbsp; ${comp.join(' &nbsp;∪&nbsp; ')}<br><span style="font-size:0.82rem;color:#5a3fa0">(the complement automaton is the union of every class product disjoint from L — here, the products tagged “complement”.)</span>`;
  }
  document.getElementById('nb24-preset').addEventListener('change',()=>{
    const p=PRODUCTS[+document.getElementById('nb24-preset').value];
    document.getElementById('nb24-u').value=p[0]; document.getElementById('nb24-v').value=p[1]; go();
  });
  document.getElementById('nb24-go').addEventListener('click',go);
  ['nb24-u','nb24-v'].forEach(id=>document.getElementById(id).addEventListener('keyup',e=>{if(e.key==='Enter')go();}));
  go();
})();
</script>
```

This is the whole complementation theorem in miniature: no state-flipping trick (that failed back in **[Notebook 16](16-dba-vs-nba-gap.qmd)**), but a finite algebra of class products, each decided in or out by an emptiness test, with the "out" ones assembled into a Büchi automaton for $\overline{L(\mathcal A)}$. Decidable inclusion — and hence $\omega$-regular model checking — follows.
